targetAudience.primary: Engineers maintaining progressively loaded agent skills, tools and plugin bundles
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands modular skill packages, routing and token optimization.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A smaller skill bundle may inherit the old capability name even after compression breaks routes, public entries or behavior.

whyNow: SkillZip Pro reports useful token reductions under protected compression and a sharp accuracy loss under an aggressive unprotected configuration, making preservation contracts an immediate engineering concern.

externalHook.description: The study reports about 38% bundle-token and 10.4% per-run reductions without reported quality loss in its protected harness, while a 71% aggressive configuration loses up to 26 accuracy points.

coreProposition: Progressive skill compression must preserve public callable entries, route reachability, resource classifications and version/provenance; routing evidence is necessary but not sufficient for semantic, permission or effect equivalence.

originalValue.description: Turns source-reported optimization results into a staged candidate lifecycle with separate structural and behavioral evidence.

readerTakeaway: Adopt a compressed skill only as a new version after route/entry audits and bounded behavioral validation pass; never let token savings or ancestry silently confer equivalence.

supported: The study models skills as progressively loaded directory bundles.
Its protected setup reports about 38% bundle-token and 10.4% per-run reductions with no reported quality loss in the evaluated harness.
Its aggressive 71% configuration reports losses of up to 26 accuracy points and the protected setup reports near-perfect route/public-entry preservation.
unsupported: Independent validation of the reported results
uncertain: Required behavioral sample size after route-preserving transformations
A portable contract for permissions and side effects

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article draws general engineering implications from a published skill-compression study.

decisionReason: The protected and aggressive cases support a concrete lifecycle rule while leaving the study's scope and independence limits explicit.
